text: Python gives you several clean ways to walk a sequence backwards.
The reversed function returns a lazy iterator that yields items from last to first.
It doesn't build a new list, it just steps through the original in reverse order.
[chuckle] Slicing with a step of negative one is the other classic way — and it does make a new list.
That same slice trick reverses a string too, since strings are sequences of characters.
[sniff] So python spelled backwards falls out in a single, tidy expression.
You can combine reversed with enumerate to number items as you count down through them.
[sigh] Reach for reversed when you want to loop efficiently, and the slice when you want an actual reversed copy.
[groan] Both read cleanly, so pick whichever makes your intent most obvious to the next reader.
